session.question: How do digital tools in environmental education foster sustainability awareness among learners?
session.answer:
Digital tools foster sustainability awareness by making environmental issues more concrete, interactive, and accessible. In environmental education, virtual reality and other digital media are used to teach topics such as climate change, helping learners better understand environmental processes and strengthening concern for planetary sustainability. The main reported effect is increased awareness and concern, indicating that digital tools can improve both environmental learning gains and sustainability consciousness. (hajjhassan2024environmentaleducationa chunk 1)

They also support sustainability awareness by enabling collaborative, transnational knowledge production. In EcoCOIL, digital platforms connect students, educators, experts, policy makers, business leaders, and community organizations across countries and disciplines, allowing co-created learning, coalition-building, and real-time engagement with sustainability problems. This participatory structure is intended to promote environmental citizenship, sustainable attitudes, and community-based action. (adefila2021ecologizedcollaborativeonline chunk 1)

Digital learning can further strengthen sustainability education by mediating the effects of collaboration and innovation on digital literacy. In the Indonesian study, digital learning in early childhood directly contributed to sustainability education and served as a key mechanism linking collaboration and innovation to sustainability understanding. This suggests that digital competence can translate into broader awareness of sustainability issues. (sari2024strengtheningdigitalliteracy chunk 1)

More broadly, digital and multimedia tools foster sustainability literacy by expanding learners’ meaning-making through multimodal and embodied forms of communication. By providing semiotic resources beyond text, digital media help learners interpret environmental signs in context and support pro-sustainability behavior. (campbell2021a“strong”approach chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-9f156f6e: The review reports that evidence-based studies in environmental education use various digital tools to promote environmental learning gains and improve sustainability awareness. Based on 21 articles from 2013–2023, the findings indicate that digital tools—especially virtual reality—are being used to teach environmental topics, with climate change being the most common focus. The main effect described is a positive impact on students’ concern for the planet’s sustainability, suggesting that digital tools help learners better understand environmental issues and become more aware of sustainability.
From Mira Hajj-Hassan, Rawad Chaker, and Anne‐Marie Cederqvist. Environmental education: a systematic review on the use of digital tools for fostering sustainability awareness. Sustainability, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su16093733, doi:10.3390/su16093733.

pqac-41912647: The paper argues that digital resources and online collaboration can support democratization of knowledge production and more equitable citizen participation in Education for Sustainable Development. It develops EcoCOIL, a model based on Collaborative Online International Learning, to expand coalition-building and promote environmental citizenship. Digital tools help connect learners across countries and disciplines, enabling co-created knowledge sharing among students, staff, experts, business leaders, policy makers, and community organizations. This transnational, participatory online approach is intended to strengthen sustainable environmental attitudes, practical action, and community-based sustainable behavior in real time.
From Arinola Adefila, Osman Arrobbio, Geraldine Brown, Zoë Robinson, Gary Spolander, Ilkhom Soliev, Bret Willers, Luca Morini, Darío Padovan, and Katherine Wimpenny. Ecologized collaborative online international learning: tackling wicked sustainability problems through education for sustainable development. Journal of Teacher Education for Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.2478/jtes-2021-0004, doi:10.2478/jtes-2021-0004.

pqac-32469f74: The paper argues that digital resources can support the democratization of knowledge production and improve equitable citizen participation in Education for Sustainable Development. It uses Collaborative Online International Learning (COIL) to develop an EcoCOIL model that expands coalition-building tools and principles. Through transnational collaboration in digital spaces, EcoCOIL connects students, staff, experts, business leaders, social innovators, policy makers, and community organizations. Its mechanisms include co-created wisdom sharing across intercultural, intergenerational, and transdisciplinary actors, integration of lifelong learning principles, and practical facilitation of sustainable behavior within communities in real time. These features are intended to build environmental citizenship and multi-layered communities of practice.
From Arinola Adefila, Osman Arrobbio, Geraldine Brown, Zoë Robinson, Gary Spolander, Ilkhom Soliev, Bret Willers, Luca Morini, Darío Padovan, and Katherine Wimpenny. Ecologized collaborative online international learning: tackling wicked sustainability problems through education for sustainable development. Journal of Teacher Education for Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.2478/jtes-2021-0004, doi:10.2478/jtes-2021-0004.

pqac-0c0c05b8: The excerpt discusses a 2024 study on strengthening digital literacy in Indonesia through collaboration, innovation, digital learning in early childhood (DLEC), and sustainability education (SE). It finds significant associations between collaboration/innovation and DLEC, and shows that DLEC plays a key mediating role in positively influencing sustainability education. The study concludes that digital learning not only mediates these relationships but also directly contributes to improving sustainability understanding, supporting the idea that digital tools can help learners develop sustainability awareness in environmental education contexts.
From Gema Ika Sari, Shinta Winasis, Ika Pratiwi, Uli Wildan Nuryanto, and Basrowi Basrowi. Strengthening digital literacy in indonesia: collaboration, innovation, and sustainability education. Social Sciences & Humanities Open, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ssaho.2024.101100, doi:10.1016/j.ssaho.2024.101100.

pqac-0b257d03: The excerpt argues that digital and multimedia learning can support sustainability literacy when understood through an embodied, semiotic lens. It says learning is grounded in environmental and bodily affordances, and that digital tools work by offering semiotic resources and multimodal forms of communication that learners interpret and use in context. The paper connects biosemiotics with critical media literacy, suggesting that digital media can increase environmental literacy and pro-sustainability behavior by expanding meaning-making beyond traditional text, and by situating learners in an Umwelt where the environment is experienced as semiosic and interactive.
From Cary Campbell, Nataša Lacković, and Alin Olteanu. A “strong” approach to sustainability literacy: embodied ecology and media. Philosophies, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/philosophies6010014, doi:10.3390/philosophies6010014.

contexts.context: The excerpt discusses digital learning as an educational format that supports sustainable education, especially highlighted during the 2020 pandemic when teaching shifted rapidly from classroom to online formats. It reports a systematic literature review and a survey of 173 university students showing that online learning experiences depend on factors such as the characteristics of online classes, support from schools and professors, and comparisons between online and face-to-face classes. The paper argues that digital learning has central importance in sustainability debates because it can help design educational models that contribute to sustainable education and shape future learning and society.

However, no digital tools are discussed in the excerpt.

Using effective tools in education may improve how these harder topics are taught and raise awareness of global challenges and sustainable development.

session.formatted_answer:
Question: How do digital tools in environmental education foster sustainability awareness among learners?

Digital tools foster sustainability awareness by making environmental issues more concrete, interactive, and accessible. In environmental education, virtual reality and other digital media are used to teach topics such as climate change, helping learners better understand environmental processes and strengthening concern for planetary sustainability. The main reported effect is increased awareness and concern, indicating that digital tools can improve both environmental learning gains and sustainability consciousness. (hajjhassan2024environmentaleducationa chunk 1)

They also support sustainability awareness by enabling collaborative, transnational knowledge production. In EcoCOIL, digital platforms connect students, educators, experts, policy makers, business leaders, and community organizations across countries and disciplines, allowing co-created learning, coalition-building, and real-time engagement with sustainability problems. This participatory structure is intended to promote environmental citizenship, sustainable attitudes, and community-based action. (adefila2021ecologizedcollaborativeonline chunk 1)

Digital learning can further strengthen sustainability education by mediating the effects of collaboration and innovation on digital literacy. In the Indonesian study, digital learning in early childhood directly contributed to sustainability education and served as a key mechanism linking collaboration and innovation to sustainability understanding. This suggests that digital competence can translate into broader awareness of sustainability issues. (sari2024strengtheningdigitalliteracy chunk 1)

More broadly, digital and multimedia tools foster sustainability literacy by expanding learners’ meaning-making through multimodal and embodied forms of communication. By providing semiotic resources beyond text, digital media help learners interpret environmental signs in context and support pro-sustainability behavior. (campbell2021a“strong”approach chunk 1)
